articles.title: White House lifts tariffs on some Canadian goods as midterm elections loom
articles.description: From 30 October, tariffs will be eased on some products, including certain machinery, and placed on others, such as carpets.
articles.summary: Canada and the US are currently locked in a tit-for-tat trade war The Trump administration is lifting some of its 50% tariffs on Canadian goods two weeks before the midterm elections, after a Republican candidate in a key Senate race said she had lobbied for the change.
key_points: Starting on 30 October, tariffs will be eased on products including "plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment," the White House said on Friday.
Republican Senator Susan Collins, who is in a tight race to keep her seat in Maine, first announced the exemptions, saying they would help her state's agriculture industry.
The US imposed a 50% levy on $20bn (£15bn) of Canadian goods after trade talks between the two countries collapsed in August.

The chancellor will also pledge millions of pounds in spending across a range of initiatives aimed at shoring up the UK's ability to respond to evolving cyber, biological and AI-enabled threats.
"AI will transform daily life: every firm, community, hospital, school, and every aspect of our economy can benefit," John Healey said.

articles.title: 'I'm 96 and have 15 million followers': The grannies taking over TikTok
articles.description: Grandma Droniak, Nonna Gracie, Viv Truran and Barbara Costello have all found fame on social media in their later years.
articles.summary: Grandma Droniak pays for her care home fees with the money she makes from brand deals on social media Ninety-six-year-old Lillian Droniak, known as Grandma Droniak to her social media followers, went viral in June after claiming her retirement home had threatened to evict her for throwing parties.
key_points: The home later confirmed the threat, but reached a settlement with Droniak that allowed her to keep partying – but not supply alcoholic drinks.
With 15 million followers, Droniak has turned her personality into a lucrative business, earning enough from social media to cover her nursing home fees of $12,000 (£9,000) a month.
The Connecticut grandma is one of many older women finding unexpected fame online, with most of their audiences often young enough to be their grandchildren.

articles.title: AI-Enabled FP&A Orchestration: Evolution, Gaps & Pathways
articles.summary: When you watch a symphony orchestra, you can see the conductor, the musicians and the instruments, but what is really magical is the invisible architecture that keeps them together: coordination.
key_points: The conductor is FP&A itself: setting direction, owning the decision, and remaining accountable for the outcome.
The musicians are our analysts and finance teams: providing the judgement and business context that no system can ever replace.
The instruments are our AI agents and data systems: continuous, scalable, and built to run in parallel.
